clue.text: Rub out paperwork — dandy to cut back in it

indicators.note: in it says the turned-round piece goes inside the paperwork word

parts.note: bumf is British slang for tedious paperwork

indicators.note: cut back says the word for the dandy is turned round

parts.note: a fop is a dandy, a man vain about his clothes

explanation.surface: An office instruction: erase the forms, and trim the fancy man's part in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rub out' looks like erasing, but it is slang for killing. 'cut back' gives POF; 'in it' places that inside the paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang verbs meaning to murder someone, to wipe them out.

clue.text: Notable racist welcoming leaders in spiky helmets

indicators.note: welcoming means the racist takes in other letters

parts.note: a bigot is an intolerant person such as a racist

indicators.note: leaders in means the first letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: A prominent bigot shows up wearing spiked helmets.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable, as a noun, is an important person, a synonym of this informal term.

clue.text: Communist leader outlining an amendment of finest list of intentions

indicators.note: outlining means the leader's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Mao Zedong led Communist China

indicators.note: an amendment changes the word finest into a new order

explanation.surface: A Communist chief draws up changes to a list of the finest aims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' is only a link here; 'amendment of' gives NIFEST, and 'outlining' wraps the leader's name round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's published declaration of policies is a set of stated aims.

clue.text: Window in Oxford college

definitions.meaning: a bay window projecting from an upper floor
one of the colleges of Oxford University

explanation.surface: A window in an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a projecting upper-storey bay window and a college at Oxford.

clue.text: Rich confection, one's not all there

definitions.meaning: a dense cake packed with dried fruit
slang for an eccentric or mad person

explanation.surface: A rich dessert, and someone a little crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is both a heavy cake with dried fruit and slang for a crackpot.

clue.text: Bird or chap seen during the day

indicators.note: seen during says the following letters go inside the day

parts.note: Mon is the short form of Monday
he refers to a chap, a man

explanation.surface: Bird-watching: a bird, or perhaps a man, was spotted in daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common waterbird, a dark rail with a red bill.

clue.text: US city in time becoming a city in Europe

indicators.note: in puts the US city inside the time word

parts.note: min is short for minute, a unit of time
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: An American city in time turns into a European one.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major city in northern Italy, capital of Lombardy.

clue.text: Children on holiday over three months

parts.note: someone on holiday is off work
spring is a season of about three months

explanation.surface: Kids are off school on holiday for three months.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's young are their descendants, the next generation.

clue.text: 50% of 50% providing a city in the Middle East

indicators.note: fifty per cent of means take the first half of the word that follows

parts.note: fifty per cent is a half
providing means if, on condition that

explanation.surface: A sum about a quarter, perhaps, yields a Middle Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: The second '50%' gives HALF; the first '50% of' keeps half of it, HA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a port city in northern Israel, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Item of clothing just around the corner on chain

parts.note: something nigh is near, about to happen
to tie is to chain or bind

explanation.surface: A garment hanging just round the corner on a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a garment for sleeping in, worn in bed.

clue.text: Information on two bottled spirits

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Details on a couple of bottles of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottled' points to genies kept in lamps or bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Genies are magical spirits of Arabian tales, often trapped in a lamp or bottle.

clue.text: Winning line, providing time getting home good, is inspirational

parts.note: up means ahead in a game
providing means if
someone home is in

explanation.surface: A sports report: winning line, home in good time, very stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that raises the spirits is inspiring, morally or emotionally elevating.

clue.text: Pretentious filth in a university broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Smut aired on a university station, passed off as highbrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal term describes affected, pompous or high-flown language and manners.

clue.text: One working as a decoy in factory

definitions.meaning: a person placed to mislead others, like a stooge
an industrial works or manufacturing site

explanation.surface: An undercover agent posing as a decoy inside a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a planted stooge and an industrial works.

clue.text: Dip one's toe in a seed coat

parts.note: to dip a toe in is to try or test something

explanation.surface: Cautiously trying out a coat made from seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists use this term for the protective outer layer around a seed.

clue.text: Write number in as in range

indicators.note: in puts the writing and the number inside the word as

parts.note: to pen is to write
nine is a number

explanation.surface: Instructions to write a figure in, as with a range of values.
explanation.definitionFit: These mountains run down the length of Italy, forming its spine.

clue.text: Into something fruity, one getting ahead of the African party machine

indicators.note: into says the following pieces go inside the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

indicators.note: getting ahead of puts one before the party

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: A busy political picture: someone gets in front of the African party machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A household device such as a washing machine or fridge is a domestic machine.

clue.text: Negative feeling, as quiet girl brought up in semi, moving

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: in puts the turned girl inside the rearranged letters
moving means the letters of semi are rearranged
brought up, in a down clue, means the girl is read upwards

parts.note: miss is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl raised in a semi-detached house as things shift, feeling gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a British semi-detached house. 'brought up' gives SSIM and 'moving' gives EISM; 'in' sets the first within the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting the worst outcome is a gloomy, negative outlook.

clue.text: Carrying medical qualification, doctor went with our deputy

indicators.note: carrying means the rearranged letters hold the qualification
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree

explanation.surface: A qualified medic and doctor went along with our second-in-command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb, not the medic: it gives NUERTWO, and 'Carrying' holds the degree inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The second in charge, an assistant or second-in-command, is a deputy.

clue.text: 0-0, playing from memory then?

definitions.meaning: a final score with no goals on either side
a musician playing without a score, the sheet music

explanation.surface: A goalless draw, or musicians performing without sheet music.
explanation.definitionFit: A game with no goals has none on the board; a pianist without sheet music plays without a score.

clue.text: Central European region elevated in praise — listen

indicators.note: elevated says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A region raised up in praise; pay attention.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'elevated' means read upwards: AISELIS sits inside 'praise listen' and turns round. No word marks the hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: This historical region now lies mostly in southwest Poland, with parts in Czechia and Germany.

clue.text: Easy putt to achieve that's short — about one millimetre

indicators.note: about says the shortened word goes round the next letters
that's short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to get something is to achieve it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A golfer's tiny putt, short of the hole by about a millimetre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's short' cuts GET to GE, which goes 'about' I and MM.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a putt so short that opponents concede it without it being played.

clue.text: German city on the outskirts of Cologne demonstrating spirit

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr, western Germany

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A German city on the edge of Cologne shows real spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The fundamental nature or core quality of something is its spirit.

clue.text: A classic in Italian, somewhat making a comeback?

indicators.note: making a comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Italian classic enjoying a revival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' picks NITAL from 'in Italian'; 'making a comeback' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Classics as a school subject means ancient Greek and Roman language, so Rome's tongue is one.

clue.text: Ace overshadowed by red card

indicators.note: overshadowed by means the ace is covered by the red

parts.note: a Trot, short for Trotskyist, is a left-winger or red
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A card game where a red card puts an ace in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: These are cards used in fortune-telling, with a pack of major and minor arcana.

clue.text: Don't be so accusative, it's futile

definitions.meaning: an urge to point the finger less
having no purpose or chance of success

explanation.surface: A rebuke: stop pointing the finger, it achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no purpose or use is futile; read as two words, it urges less finger-pointing.

clue.text: Hear harmony in musical composition

indicators.note: hear says the word for harmony is taken by its sound

parts.note: peace is harmony, absence of strife

explanation.surface: Listen for the harmony in a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A single work of music is a composition.

clue.text: One's striped like a label?

definitions.meaning: a cat with a striped coat
jokily, resembling a tab or tag

explanation.surface: Something with stripes, like a label.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a striped cat, and fancifully means tab-like.

clue.text: Plain green salad eaten by the first group?

indicators.note: eaten by puts the tossed letters inside the group

parts.note: set I, group number one

indicators.note: a salad is a mixture, so the letters of green are tossed

explanation.surface: A simple green salad served to the first table of diners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salad' turns GREEN into RENGE, which SET I takes in after SE.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous grassland in Tanzania is a vast savanna, a plain.

clue.text: Don't declare it's a stick

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to keep batting instead of ending the innings
a short rod, such as a conductor's or relay runner's

explanation.surface: An instruction not to admit to owning a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a captain may declare, closing the innings; to bat on is to carry on batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A conductor's wand or relay runner's rod is a short stick; read as two words it means keep batting.

clue.text: Expert performer rates it absurd

indicators.note: absurd means nonsensical, so these letters are made into nonsense and rearranged

explanation.surface: A skilled entertainer thinks it's ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a professional entertainer, especially a skilled singer or dancer.

clue.text: Blossom an attractive thing, as something to dance around

parts.note: may is hawthorn blossom
a magnetic pole attracts

explanation.surface: Spring flowers and a magnet, as things to dance round.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawthorn is called may in Britain, after the month it flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: On May Day villagers dance round a tall decorated pole holding ribbons.
